author: reek
body: Known-answer test for the RelEquiJoin plan node. Three tiny tables: owners is the dimension with two rows, pets is the fact with four rows, care holds one feeding entry per owner-and-pet pair. One pet names an owner that does not exist, therefore the inner join drops that pet and three rows survive. The left child is the probe side of the hash join, therefore output rows preserve pet insertion order: Rex with Ann, Tom with Ben, Sky with Ann. The plan runs through the optimizer first and prints its explain rendering, so the optimizer's equi-join arms are exercised alongside the executor's.

author: reek
body: The second plan joins on a composite key: pets to care on owner-id and pname together. The care table carries a decoy row for owner 2 with pet name Rex. A join on owner-id alone would pair that row with Tom and answer wrong; the two-column join drops the decoy because no pet has owner 2 and name Rex at once. Three rows survive in pet insertion order: Rex eats kibble, Tom eats bones, Sky eats fish, and Zed matches nothing.

author: reek
body: Join pets to owners on the shared owner-id column, then project to the pet name and the owner name so the duplicate join column drops out immediately, in the manner the equi-join contract requires. The composite plan joins pets to care on owner-id and pname together and projects the pet name and the food.
